messages:
maria_sales: Heads-up — Acme signed LOI pending legal. They want a 2-week Reserved Pool POC next Tuesday. Requirements: single static outbound IP (their connectors will allowlist us), a dedicated endpoint hostname, and short-lived API keys for their engs. Who owns this handoff?

ajay_se: I can run the setup. Two deployment choices for the POC: (A) Dedicated endpoint with a stable VIP (best for customer allowlists), or (B) reserve pool nodes that NAT via one or more EIPs (faster to provision). Which do they prefer?

maria_sales: They specifically asked for a single static egress IP if possible. Ops contact expected. Also they want a sample curl to validate once we give IPs/host.

nate_netops: We can provide either: a single VIP (FQDN + one IP) for Dedicated Endpoint, or up to 4 EIPs for NAT if they want redundancy. Lead times: EIP reservation ~24h, VIP assignment + DNS ~30-60m after deploy. I need ticket with customer tag + POC start/end dates.

caroline_cs: Security note: we record outbound flow metadata and can include egress IP in traces. For the questionnaire: we can produce a CSV export of outbound requests for the POC. If they require mutual TLS to their partner endpoints, we can present client certs from the nodes.

maria_sales: @nate_netops can you drop a sample allowlist block they can paste into their firewall? Also, do we need a legal SLA addendum for a short POC?

nate_netops: Sample allowlist (suggested):
```
# Acme POC outbound IPs (example)
18.205.60.2/32
52.14.211.99/32
3.129.45.200/32
```
I'll file the EIP ticket now. No additional SLA for 2-week POC unless customer requests.

ajay_se: For the API keys: we'll create a project-scoped key with a 14-day TTL and mark it "poc-acme". Keys are hosted in our key store by default. If they require KMS-backed keys for Private later, that's a separate path.

ryan_finance: Pricing flag: mark this as internal short-term POC discount. Sales: include a note in the quote and I'll approve the override.

maria_sales: Perfect. Draft onboarding email I'll send to their ops contact (kevin@acme.com) — will include the allowlist, the curl snippet, contact for network handoff, and the TTL for the key.

ajay_se: Curl to validate once DNS/IP is in place (include bearer placeholder):
```bash
curl -i "https://acme-poc.rdinfr.dev/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer POC_KEY_HERE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

caroline_cs: Add this data handling blurb: POC request/trace logs retained for 30 days and then purged unless otherwise agreed. Security follow-ups can go to security@redwood.ai.

deploy-bot: reserved-pool created — pool-id: pool-1147, region: us-west-2 (requested by maria_sales)

nate_netops: EIP reservation submitted. Will post exact IPs + ticket id when allocated. Please send final POC window in the ticket.

kevin_acme: Thanks all — we've raised our firewall change request referencing your sample block, ticket #ACME-9876. Will confirm when accepted.

maria_sales: Great, once kevin confirms I'll generate the POC key and share the curl + final IPs. :thumbsup:

nate_netops: Follow-up (allocated EIPs): 18.205.60.2, 52.14.211.99, 3.129.45.200. Ticket id: NET-4521. They can be treated as a single IP set or used with NAT translation depending on customer firewall rules.

ajay_se: Note for future: migrating this POC to Private adds ~3-5 days due to KMS/VPC peering work. Flag that to Acme if they want production parity.

maria_sales: Thank you — I'll post the handoff email now and update the pipeline.

caroline_cs: I'll prepare the short answers for their security questionnaire and attach the CSV export example.

maria_sales: Closing loop — keep me posted in this thread if anything changes.
